seed_vocabulary.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
seed_vocabulary.prose: The precedence ordering of instruction sources from highest to lowest: Root > System > Developer > User > Guideline > (No Authority). This ordering determines which instructions override which when conflicts arise.

seed_vocabulary.name: applicable_instructions
seed_vocabulary.prose: Instructions that must be followed, determined by filtering all candidate instructions to exclude those that are misaligned with higher-authority instructions, superseded by later same-level instructions, or suspected to be mistaken. These form the actual guidance the assistant follows.

seed_vocabulary.name: misaligned_instruction
seed_vocabulary.prose: An instruction that is in conflict with either the letter or implied intent of a higher-authority instruction. Misaligned instructions are filtered out when determining what the assistant should actually do.

seed_vocabulary.name: scope_of_autonomy
seed_vocabulary.prose: A clear, mutually understood boundary that defines which sub-goals the assistant may pursue, acceptable side effects, and when the assistant must pause for clarification or approval. This prevents misunderstandings about what autonomy the assistant has in pursuing multi-step goals.

seed_vocabulary.name: letter_and_spirit_principle
seed_vocabulary.prose: The principle that the assistant should respect not just the literal wording of instructions but also their underlying intent, context, plausible implicit goals of stakeholders, and the higher-level purpose the instructions serve. Guides interpretation of ambiguous, inconsistent, or indirectly stated instructions.

judgment_calls: Chose L290→L291 (after examples in 'Follow all applicable instructions') over L203 (after the misalignment definition) because L290 represents the complete cycle: definitions + rules + worked examples demonstrating the rules. Cutting at L203 would split examples from their rule foundation, requiring children to carry loose example citations.

Chose L525→L526 (after 'Act within scope' examples) over L390 (between 'Respect letter and spirit' and 'No other objectives') because L426-L488 ('No other objectives' + 'Act within scope') form a paired constraint on autonomy: first, what goals to pursue; second, what scope of pursuit is allowed. 'Respect letter and spirit' (L292-L389) is about interpretation strategy, not autonomy constraints—separating constraints from interpretation strategy splits their conceptual coherence.

Did not make finer cuts (e.g., splitting 'Control side effects' from 'Assume best intentions' and 'Ignore untrusted data') despite child 3 being 270 lines, because all three subsections form a unified risk-mitigation strategy: (1) minimize unintended consequences via proportionate action, (2) assume users mean well and grant intellectual freedom, (3) assume embedded instructions are untrusted by default. Separating them would require new seeds for 'side_effects_principle', 'best_intentions_principle', 'untrusted_data_framework', and complicate the cross-link graph without thematic benefit—each child feeds forward into the next.

Passing letter_and_spirit_principle as a new seed (not inherited) because it is established uniquely within my child 2, used by my child 3, and not mentioned or seeded by the parent division at c2. The parent seeded the authority and scope concepts child 1-2 need, but this principle-of-interpretation concept was not on its radar.
